clinician.trajectory_summary: A 23-year-old male presented with 9 months of chronic symptoms including watery diarrhea, abdominal pain, weight loss, nocturnal fever, multiple skin ulcers, painful nodules on lower limbs, glans ulcers, and arthralgia. Initial workup included colonoscopy showing shallow ulcers. A biopsy of a lower limb skin ulcer revealed an epithelioid granulomatous process with palisade granulomas and central caseous necrosis. Further microbiological analysis of this biopsy confirmed the presence of acid-fast bacilli by Ziehl-Neelsen staining and a positive culture for Mycobacterium tuberculosis, establishing the diagnosis of cutaneous tuberculosis. Histopathological analysis of intestinal biopsies showed only mild inflammatory infiltrate without bacilli, ruling out intestinal tuberculosis.

key_supporting_evidence.claim: Patient presented with chronic systemic symptoms and multiple skin lesions, including ulcers and painful nodules.
Histopathological examination of a lower limb skin ulcer revealed an epithelioid granulomatous process with palisade granulomas and central caseous necrosis.
Acid-fast bacilli (AFB) were identified by Ziehl-Neelsen staining from the skin ulcer biopsy.
Culture from the skin ulcer biopsy was positive for Mycobacterium tuberculosis.
